framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, proposed amendments (Annex A 'Proposed Changes' to DIFCA Consultation Paper No. 3, June 2026; draft cover 'Consolidated Version No. 3, in force on [XX 2026]'; NOT enacted as seen on 2026-10-16)
clause_or_page: Proposed Reg. 10.3.2(b), Annex A printed p.13 (current 10.3.2(b) would become 10.3.2(c))
requirement_paraphrase: Proposed: no one may use, operate or offer for commercial use a System that processes personal data unless the System has been tested for safety verification, including native regulatory and security design (in addition to human-defined purposes and design compliance with Reg. 10.3.1 and Commissioner audit, governance or certification requirements).
what_is_tested: Safety of the System, including regulatory and security design

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.4.4 (s2.4 Operational Security), printed p.14
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must secure its AI/ML systems through comprehensive testing and validation that gives assurance of their resilience against potential threats.
what_is_tested: Security and resilience of AI/ML systems against threats
who_tests: The entity in scope under s1.2: ministries and federal authorities and non-government CII entities; for emirate government entities verifiers read s1.2 differently (directly only where no emirate CIIP programme exists, or directly or through the Emirate Lead). See UAE-Federal-P3-08.

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories measure detection accuracy (e.g. error rates) on varied samples, including other systems' content and data not used in training, across content length, size, diversity and semantics; they also test robustness to common processing operations (compression, cropping, paraphrasing, translation, print-and-scan) and to adversarial attacks (copying, removal, regeneration, modification of marks) using the same metrics; compliance is demonstrated before market placement and over the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Reliability and robustness metrics for watermark/marking detection

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories obtain assurance that security mitigations meet the Security Goal through independent external security reviews where internal expertise is inadequate, frequent red-teaming of network and physical access management, competitive bug bounties for public-facing endpoints, periodic personnel integrity testing, third-party security reporting channels, endpoint/intrusion detection tools and a security incident response team.
what_is_tested: Security assurance testing of model and infrastructure
who_tests: Signatory provider; independent external security reviewers

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Design the evaluation protocol, write evaluation code, run and track results, and debug the evaluation; common bugs include degraded serving; evaluation cheating and evaluation awareness are listed as bugs tagged [Emerging Practice].

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems conforming to harmonised standards (or parts) whose references are published in the OJ are presumed to meet the Section 2 requirements to the extent the standards cover them.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Member States may allow real-world testing outside sandboxes of AI-enabled products under Annex I Section B legislation, through national frameworks that require a mandatory testing plan agreed with the authority and apply most Art. 60 safeguards.
what_is_tested: Real-world testing of Section B products

framework: China - Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (Doc. No. Guoxinban Tongzi [2025] No. 2; in force 1 Sep 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: On user request, providers may supply generated content without explicit labels after the user agreement sets out the user's labelling obligations and responsibility for use, and must keep related logs, including recipient information, for at least six months.

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Toolkit self-assessment tool (Digital Dubai)
clause_or_page: Page section 'What is the self-assessment tool for?'
requirement_paraphrase: The page advises against implementing an AI system unless a certain level of ethics performance is reached; 'should' guidelines weigh more than 'should consider' guidelines in the score.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Security > Security risks > Using AI > Data and model poisoning
requirement_paraphrase: To counter data and model poisoning, model outputs should be tested against known good responses and systematically tested for bias.
what_is_tested: Output integrity against known-good responses; bias
who_tests: Not specified (passive voice); context refers to the organisation running the model

framework: UAE AI Adoption Guideline in Government Services
requirement_paraphrase: Once the model is ready, it is evaluated against acceptance criteria to confirm readiness for deployment.
what_is_tested: AI/ML model readiness against acceptance criteria before deployment
who_tests: Implementing government entity (not specified in text read)
